'''Kirk Patrick Snyder''' (born June 5, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played four seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]].

==College career==
Snyder grew up in [[Upland, California]], and spent his college career at [[University of Nevada, Reno]]. In 2004, he led the Wolf Pack to its first [[2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|Sweet 16]] in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]]. During that trip, the team beat No. 2 seed [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and No. 7 seed [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], but lost in the third round to No. 3 and eventual national runner-up [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].

==Professional career==
[[File:Kirk Snyder 2011-03-26 (6).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Snyder with [[BC Nizhny Novgorod]] in 2011]]
Snyder was drafted in the first round (16th overall) of the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]]. After one season, he was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] as part one of the largest trades in NBA history (13 players, 5 teams involved).

In New Orleans, Snyder became a starter midway through [[2005–06 NBA season|his only season]]. He scored a career-high 28 points against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and averaged nearly 20 minutes per game in 68 contests. After that, he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for a 2008 second-round draft pick and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clutchfans.net/news/1346/kirk_snyder_acquired_from_hornets/|title=Kirk Snyder acquired from Hornets|website=ClutchFans.net|access-date=6 November 2018|archive-date=November 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181107103944/http://www.clutchfans.net/news/1346/kirk_snyder_acquired_from_hornets/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 21, 2008, as he was often the last man from the Rockets' bench, Snyder was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] along with a 2010 second-round draft pick and cash considerations for [[Gerald Green]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3257573|title=Timberwolves trade Gerald Green to Rockets for Kirk Snyder|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=6 November 2018}}</ref>

His stint with the Timberwolves ended up being his last playing days in the NBA throughout his professional career. Snyder's final NBA game was played on April 16, 2008, in a 110 - 101 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] where he recorded 6 points, 3 rebounds and 2 assists. Coincidentally, Bucks' guard [[Awvee Storey]] also played his final NBA game during this matchup, recording 7 points, 4 rebounds and 1 assist.

During the 2008 off-season, Snyder signed with the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]'s [[Zhejiang Horses]].<ref>[http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-12/12/content_10497227.htm Bonzi Wells joins CBA with Shanxi Zhongyu] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081215012129/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-12/12/content_10497227.htm |date=2008-12-15 }}</ref>

Snyder later joined the [[Halifax Rainmen]] of the [[Premier Basketball League]] (PBL). After playing three games for Halifax in late January, 2011, they waived him.

In March 2011 he signed with [[BC Nizhny Novgorod]] in Russia until the end of the season,<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120731121834/http://www.championat.ru/basketball/news-755671.html|title="Нижний Новгород" подписал американского форварда Снайдера}}, Championat.ru  {{in lang|ru}}</ref> but left the team in April for personal reasons.<ref>[http://www.nn-basket.ru/news/detail.php?ID=2909 Снайдер покинул "Нижний Новгород"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309084314/http://www.nn-basket.ru/news/detail.php?ID=2909 |date=2012-03-09 }}, Nn-basket.ru {{in lang|ru}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Snyder married his college sweetheart Haley Dahl, and has three children. Haley is the cousin of [[National Football League|NFL]] offensive line guard [[Harvey Dahl]], who also attended Nevada, and played Wolf Pack football there. Snyder and Dahl have since divorced.

Snyder was arrested on March 30, 2009, after he allegedly broke into a [[Warren County, Ohio]] home and assaulted a man, sheriff deputies said.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/hp/content/oh/story/news/local/2009/03/30/pjm033009nbaarrest.html |title=Former NBA player arrested for alleged assault |access-date=2009-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090401154530/http://www.daytondailynews.com/hp/content/oh/story/news/local/2009/03/30/pjm033009nbaarrest.html |archive-date=2009-04-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://warren.miamivalleyjails.org/JAILBOOKING.ASPX?CJIS_OR_PARTY_ID=C10554847&JAILBOOKING_ID=5256491 |title=Warren County, Ohio - Persons Currently in Custody |access-date=2009-03-31 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222143633/http://warren.miamivalleyjails.org/JAILBOOKING.ASPX?CJIS_OR_PARTY_ID=C10554847&JAILBOOKING_ID=5256491 |archive-date=2012-02-22 }}</ref> He was charged with aggravated [[burglary]]; he pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity at a March 31, 2009 hearing and was held on $500,000 [[bail]].<ref>[https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20090331/ap_on_sp_bk_ne/bkn_former_nba_player_charges;_ylt=Ano7_j8vFXnwkxApXYXXSS4LMxIF Former NBA Player Charged with Burglary] Yahoo! Sports, March 31, 2009</ref>

He was subsequently convicted and sentenced to three years in jail and fined $5,550 in restitution. He was released early and signed with the [[Halifax Rainmen]] in Canada. [[Andre Levingston]], the owner of the team, said, "Everybody makes mistakes, but I don't think they should be crucified for the rest of their life. You pay your debt to society and you humble yourself and you learn from your mistakes. So everybody deserves a second chance, maybe a third chance."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rgj.com/article/20110126/SPORTS06/101260409/1018/sports|title=Nevada basketball notes: Out of jail, Snyder joins Canadian league basketball team|website=Rgj.com|access-date=6 November 2018}}</ref>
